video.title: He Can't Code but His AI Agents Make Him $5K/Month

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Vadim, an 18-year-old non-coder who vibe-coded Vugola, an all-in-one clipping, scheduling and captioning SaaS, using Claude Code, Supabase, Vercel and GitHub. He claims $5K revenue in 30 days at ~80% margin, with 267 paying users on $9/$39/$99 plans, acquired mainly via Twitter after Reddit/X outreach by an OpenClaw agent. He also describes running a small team of Hermes agents (CEO, marketing, growth, coding, support) and shares prompting tips, PostHog analytics, Paperclip, and mind-mapping for niche research. Key takeaway: a solo founder can build and run a niche SaaS with AI agents cheaply, but the numbers are self-reported and the product is still in beta.

speakers.name: Vadim
speakers.description: 18-year-old founder of Vugola, a non-technical vibe coder; Twitter handle partially given as Vadem_strizhes

ideas.name: Vugola - all-in-one AI clipping, scheduling and captioning SaaS
ideas.one_liner: Subscription web app that turns long videos into short clips, captions them and schedules posts, aimed at clippers, podcasters and marketers.
ideas.business_model: Monthly subscription tiers with credits, plus quarterly/yearly upsells and one-off credit packs
ideas.customer: Clippers, podcasters, streamers, entrepreneurs, affiliate marketers and smaller creators who need short-form clips
ideas.problem: Existing clipping tools (e.g. Opus Clip) are seen as expensive, slow, and reuse the same clip moments across multiple clips, wasting credits
ideas.offer: Clip long-form video using Gemini transcript and visual analysis (face tracking, cropping, speaker emotion), then caption and schedule natively in one tool; built to be agent-friendly

pricing.model: Three monthly paid tiers, no free plan; checkout upsells to quarterly plan and extra credit packs
pricing.notes: Free plan removed around end of Feb because users farmed free credits with multiple accounts; $9 minimum acted as a filter and sales started. Popup upsell from monthly to quarterly, then custom checkout upselling credit packs; one day reached about $900 after adding upsells.

acquisition_channels.details: Building in public on Twitter/X; purely X for the last two months, personal brand ~27,000 followers; now starting Instagram, YouTube Shorts and TikTok.

quote.text: purely on X in the last two months when I actually started marketing it
quote.speaker: Vadim

acquisition_channels.details: OpenClaw marketing agent scanned Reddit, LinkedIn and X for people complaining about clipping tools or Opus Clip (e.g. during a 48-hour outage), produced a list of usernames and posts, and Vadim DMed them offering free trial. Got ~450 free users and lots of feedback. Manual DMs to individuals may breach PECR in the UK.

quote.text: give me a list like bullet bullet bullet their usernames the post where they're complaining so I can go and shoot them a DM
quote.speaker: Vadim

acquisition_channels.details: In talks with Content Rewards founder about an API/agent-friendly integration so agent clippers can use Vugola and submit clips to campaigns.

ideas.delivery: Software delivered via web app; clip generation runs on Gemini API credits (transcript and video analysis). Built and maintained by Vadim with Claude Code and Codex plus a team of Hermes agents.
unit_economics_claims: ~$400-600/month spent on AI coding and agent subscriptions
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated explicitly; ongoing Claude Max about $200/month plus a second Codex plan (~$200/month), agents ~$400-600/month total; spent ~$500 of Lovable credits in 4 days early on
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Started building Oct/Nov; first sale around Feb 2 (about 3-4 months); first full month (March) about $5,000

acquisition.how: Twitter content is human-led. Agent-found social posts and manual DMs are cold outreach that is risky under PECR for individuals; inbound channels (SEO, app listings, paid ads, content) could be automated.

onboarding.how: Self-serve SaaS signup and Stripe checkout; he admits no onboarding or offboarding flows were set up initially, but they can be built in-app with agents.

delivery.how: Clips are produced by software with Gemini and API credits; agents and Claude Code maintain the product with occasional human oversight.

billing.how: Stripe subscriptions and upsells run unattended.

support.how: He claims a customer support agent and PostHog monitoring via cron jobs, but quality is unverified and a human still handles escalations.

uk_applicability.notes: SaaS and Stripe work the same in the UK. Cold DM outreach to individuals needs care under PECR/GDPR; handle VAT and platform terms for social scheduling.

risks: Self-reported, unverified numbers; product in beta
Competes with Opus Clip, which raised $50M
Churn typically in 1-3 months; no conversion/retention data set up early
Heavy dependence on Gemini API costs and credit pricing; margins could erode
Reliance on Twitter alone as a channel
Platform API/policy changes for scheduling and clipping
Frequent free-credit abuse before the paywall

tactics.name: Replace the free plan with a $9 minimum paid plan
steps: Launch with a free plan to gather feedback
Notice credit abuse from multiple free accounts and almost no paid conversions
Remove the free plan and set a $9/month minimum
Use the price as a filter for real users; sales started right after

quote.text: I'm not going to have any free plans I'm going to make like the $9 plan like minimum
quote.speaker: Vadim

tactics.name: Stack upsells at checkout
steps: Offer monthly and yearly plans
When a user clicks monthly, show a popup selling a quarterly plan
After plan selection, send to a custom checkout page that upsells a one-off pack of extra credits
Aim to extract more revenue before typical 1-3 month churn

quote.text: you want to keep upselling them like better better deals maximizing how much revenue you can take
quote.speaker: Vadim

tactics.name: Agent-driven social listening for early users
steps: Build a marketing agent with keywords tied to the niche
Scan Reddit, LinkedIn and X for complaints about competitors
Have it list usernames and links to the posts
DM those users offering a free trial and collect feedback
Check UK PECR rules before copying this for individuals

quote.text: look for users complaining about Opus Clip because even Opus Clip back in the day they had like a 48 hour outage
quote.speaker: Vadim

tactics.name: Competitor review mining with a browser agent
steps: Test all competitors yourself
Have an agent with Chrome DevTools MCP open tabs, screenshot and click through products
Read customer reviews for complaints (price, slow processing, duplicate clips)
Aim to make your product about 10% better and niche down to smaller creators

tactics.name: The 'let them cook' autonomy skill
steps: Give agents the tools and a dummy account logins they need
Write a custom skill telling the agent to finish tasks no matter what and self-improve on blockers
Only ping the human when the task is done or help is truly needed
Ask the agent what MCP servers and API keys it needs to be autonomous

quote.text: you work on it no matter what, you do not bug me at all until you like figure it out
quote.speaker: Vadim

tactics.name: Reverse prompting and rich context
steps: Tell the agent your goals and ask it to ask you questions back
Keep notes on designs you like and screenshot them for the AI
Be specific rather than saying 'copy xyz.com'
Treat bad AI output as a context problem

quote.text: you want it to ask you questions back
quote.speaker: Vadim

tactics.name: Set up PostHog event tracking via agent
steps: Create a free PostHog account and get an API key
Have the agent embed the code in the app
Brainstorm events with the agent: signup, first clip, first download, first post, first caption, cancel
Track the whole user journey and conversion from the start

tactics.name: Niche research with mind mapping
steps: Spend one to two weeks researching a market yourself
Understand competitors and where the future is headed
Mind-map (e.g. Miro) how ideas connect, e.g. automated leads to agentic leads
Become the expert in the niche

quote.text: I would not recommend Lovable at all.
quote.speaker: Vadim

warnings.warning: OpenClaw had poor memory, contradictory behaviour and little visibility into what it was doing.

quote.text: I found myself repeating to openclaw time and time again
quote.speaker: Vadim

warnings.warning: Buying Claude through the mobile app costs more (about $250 vs $200) because of Apple's cut; buy on the web.
Revenue is only one month old and self-reported; churn typically occurs within 1-3 months so durability is unproven.

lessons.lesson: Pick one complex, durable software problem and go deep instead of shipping many throwaway apps.

quote.text: people build 10 apps and they just like quote unquote throw crap on the wall and just see whatever sticks
quote.speaker: Vadim

lessons.lesson: Mine competitor reviews and test their products to find gaps (price, speed, duplicated outputs) and aim to be modestly better in a niche.
A low paid entry price can validate demand better than a free plan and filters out freeloaders.
Upsells at checkout (longer plans, credit packs) raise revenue per user given early churn.
Non-technical founders can ship real software with a small stack (Claude Code, Supabase, Vercel, GitHub) if they supply detailed context.
Bad AI output is usually a context and prompting problem; be specific, use screenshots and let the agent ask questions.

quote.text: if AI gives you something bad, it's a skill issue cuz AI can only act on the minor context
quote.speaker: Vadim

lessons.lesson: Design products to be agent-usable (APIs, skills) since agents may become buyers and users of software.
Set up analytics and funnel tracking early, even if launch speed matters more.
Persistence through months of failed builds before first revenue (Oct to Feb) was key.

quote.text: I could have quit along the way, but I'm like, "No, I'm going to put my head down.
quote.speaker: Vadim

lessons.lesson: A small agent team can substitute for several salaried roles at a few hundred dollars a month, but subscription token economics may not persist.
Build in public on one channel (X) to get first customers before diversifying.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with specific figures (revenue, tiers, user count, margin), but all are unverified, only about one month of revenue, a very young product, and margin/cost detail is vague. Conversion and churn data were admittedly missing.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Vadim sells Vugola and promotes it; host plugs Beehiiv (sponsor) and TK Owners community.
